newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Vishay cancels $50 mln Israel plant.
newsitem.headline: Vishay cancels $50 mln Israel plant.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology has cancelled its plans to build a $50 million plant in the Israeli development town of Ofakim, a company spokeswoman said.

"The president of Vishay Israel, Abraham Inbar, has advised the Investment Centre under instructions from the head office in the United States that the company has decided to cancel plans to set up a plant in Ofakim," spokesman Merav Ratan said.
"Vishay will make the investment in another country," she said, declining to give further details.
Vishay Intertechnology president Felix Zandman has been quoted as saying the company was considering setting up the plant in the Czech Republic.
Vishay's plans for expansion at its existing Israeli plants in Dimona, Beersheba and Migdal Haemek will continue and are not affected by the decision to cancel the new plant, the spokeswoman said.
The decision to cancel the Ofakim plant is the result of the government Investment Centre's failure so far to approve the plan.
Early this year then prime minister Shimon Peres asked Vishay to set up a project in Ofakim following the shutdown of a textile plant. Ofakim has the highest unemployment rate in Israel.

Vishay applied for a 34 percent government investment grant but the Investment Centre has delayed approving new projects because it ran out of funding. Last week the parliamentary finance committee approved a 300 million shekel increase in the 1996 budget.
Officials at the Investment Centre could not immediately be reached for comment.
Vishay, a Pennsylvania-based maker of passive electronic components, has three facilities in Israel with annual sales of $300 million.
